title: Authoring queue
summary: One paper in, one checked benchmark out. For each PDF in the inbox a fresh agent reads the paper, writes benchmark.json, digitizes the reference curves, runs the solver and compares the result with the paper, then stops in one of three states: done, needs_you or failed. It is not unattended: when a figure can't be read the run parks and waits for a person, and only a person promotes a finished benchmark into the corpus.

groups.label: for each PDF in the inbox
groups.detail: One pass over the inbox. --loop repeats passes; --pdf runs a single paper outside the queue.

groups.label: agent session (one attempt)
groups.detail: Claude Code by default, or DeepSeek Harness with --harness dsh. Follows WORKER.md phase by phase, with a wall clock (TIMEOUT) and a turn limit (MAX_TURNS) as backstops.

nodes.label: PDF inbox
nodes.detail: Drop papers here. The file name becomes the run's slug.

nodes.label: One-off paper
nodes.detail: A URL or path given with --pdf. Runs in dryrun/, outside the queue, so it can never be promoted by accident.

nodes.label: Preflight
nodes.detail: Tools, skills and schema present, pymupdf and pillow in the venv, a Linux claude CLI on PATH, the inbox exists. A failing import oofem only warns: Phases 1 to 3 work without it.

nodes.label: Queue decision
nodes.detail: Human data found in the workdir: reset attempts and dispatch. done or failed: skip. needs_you: skip unless --resume. Attempts above MAX_ATTEMPTS: skip. Password-protected PDF: recorded as done/infeasible, no agent.

nodes.label: Workdir + prompt
nodes.detail: Copies the PDF into its workdir and fills the {{...}} placeholders in WORKER.md with absolute paths, the attempt number and the solver timeout.

nodes.label: Dispatch agent
nodes.detail: Starts a fresh agent with the prompt and the workdir. Both dispatchers look the same to the queue: the final message on stdout, a timeout or crash in the exit code.

nodes.label: 0 · Resume check
nodes.detail: Picks up whatever an earlier attempt left on disk, including the fix-iteration count.

nodes.label: 1 · Feasibility
nodes.detail: Reads the paper in page ranges and builds a table of parameters with sources. Decides FEASIBLE or NOT_FEASIBLE.

nodes.label: 2 · Author benchmark.json
nodes.detail: Writes the spec following CREATE.md and the physics modules, then checks it with check_benchmark.py.

nodes.label: 3 · Extract reference data
nodes.detail: An AI digitizer driven through Claude in Chrome (EXTRACT-WEB.md) reads the paper's figures into CSVs. Chrome must be open and connected.

nodes.label: 3a · Hand to a human
nodes.detail: When a figure can't be digitized, leaves CSV templates and parks the run as needs_you.

nodes.label: 3b · Ingest human data
nodes.detail: Reshapes whatever the person dropped in (any layout) into the reference format.

nodes.label: 4 · Run
nodes.detail: timeout SOLVER_TIMEOUT thcm oofem <case> --remesh. An error caused by the JSON is fixed at the cost of one fix iteration; a pipeline bug stops the run as failed.

nodes.label: 5 · Analyze
nodes.detail: Compares the result with the paper's data following ANALYSIS.md and states the match within a tolerance it names.

nodes.label: 6 · Bounded fix
nodes.detail: One fix from the whitelist per iteration: units, axis calibration, probe coordinates, schema errors, dt strategy, BC values transcribed wrong. Tuning material parameters to improve the fit is forbidden.

nodes.label: 7 · Terminate
nodes.detail: Writes RESULT.md and records the stop with status.py: done (verdict reproduced, not_reproduced or infeasible), needs_you, or failed.

nodes.label: Crash handling
nodes.detail: The agent exited without a terminal or parked status (timeout, turn limit, crash). The run is recorded as failed and the previous status kept as STATUS.attemptN.json. failed is terminal, so later passes skip it.

nodes.label: status.json + RESULT.md
nodes.detail: State, verdict, a one-line key result, the phase log and the attempt count. RESULT.md says what matched, what didn't and why, and what a person should do next.

nodes.label: Queue summary
nodes.detail: One row per workdir: state/verdict, slug, phase reached, attempts, key result. Printed after every pass and by --summary.

nodes.label: Person adds data
nodes.detail: Puts the missing numbers anywhere in the case directory, in any shape, and runs the queue again.

nodes.label: Person reviews
nodes.detail: Reads RESULT.md before promoting. Promotion is the human gate into the corpus.

nodes.label: Promote
nodes.detail: promote.sh <slug>: requires done/reproduced (FORCE=1 overrides the verdict), moves the workdir to benchmarks/<slug>, drops .run/ and stages it with git add.

edges.when: the error is a JSON mistake
a mismatch has a whitelist cause

edges.label: fix and re-run
edges.carries: one whitelist correction, then check_benchmark.py, a full re-run and a fresh analysis

edges.when: no whitelist fix applies, or the 2 iterations are spent
the agent exited without a terminal or parked status

edges.carries: state failed + the agent's phase log
which file goes in which folder

edges.label: run the queue again
edges.carries: handoff.py scan finds the new data and resets attempts

params.help: Run one paper outside the queue, in dryrun/, where it can't be promoted.
Keep watching the inbox, one pass every SECONDS (default 300). Can't be combined with --pdf.
Also dispatch runs parked on a person, optionally only the one with this slug.
Which agent harness runs the session: Claude Code, or DeepSeek Harness.
Which model the dsh harness uses (see --list-models).
Permit a model that costs money. A run is hours of agent turns, not one call.
How many times one PDF may be dispatched. Human data resets the count.
Turn limit for one agent session.
Wall-clock limit for one agent session.
Wall-clock limit for one thcm run inside the session.
FORCE=1 promotes a done run whose verdict is not reproduced.
Decide and prepare everything, write the prompts, dispatch nothing.
Print the queue summary table, then exit.
List what the configured endpoint serves, then exit.
One-line description, used by worker.sh to list the jobs.
Print where the queue's workdirs live.
